exact.трамвайный билет, сложенный вчетверо: a tram ticket folded in four
exact.Вот трамвайный билет, сложенный вчетверо: Here's a tram ticket folded in four. I once wrapped somebody's phone number in it, lost the number, and the ticket stayed.
exact.У нас перемены приходили мостами и рельс: For us change came by bridges and rails: first the tram, then a new bridge over the Golden Horn, then the bridge over the Bosphorus, then the metro. At home we counted it by neighbours, every year someone came in from a village and stayed.
exact.Однажды мы с подругой сели не на тот пар: Once a friend and I got on the wrong ferry and ended up on the other shore. We only went back in the evening, we spent the whole day by the water with simit and decided that had been the plan all along.
exact.ключик от почтового ящика: a little key to a letterbox
exact.Это ключ от почтового ящика, совсем мале: This is the key to a letterbox, a tiny one. The letterbox is long gone, the house was pulled down, but I never threw the key away.
exact.Город при мне рос так быстро, что за ним: In my time the city grew so fast that neither the streets nor the buses could keep up. First the new station and the park, then whole districts of newcomers, then the metro, and every time Mum said we lived somewhere else now, though we'd never moved.
exact.Как-то зимой я поскользнулась у самого д: One winter I slipped right outside the house and sat straight down in a snowdrift with a bag of eggs. Not one egg broke, and the neighbour went round till evening telling everyone I had a charm on me.
exact.входной билет на ярмарку: an entrance ticket to the fair
exact.Входной билет на ярмарку, уже без корешк: An entrance ticket to the fair, the stub's gone. I don't remember what year, we went almost every summer.
exact.У нас каждое лето начиналось с ярмарки в: Our summer always started with the fair in the Kültürpark, that's how we counted the year. And change came from the sea and the port: a new quay being built, a university opening, and suddenly the talk at supper was all about who'd found work where.
exact.Однажды вечером мы всем домом вынесли ст: One evening the whole building carried chairs down to the bay and waited for a breeze, because indoors you couldn't breathe. The breeze never came, but we sat there till midnight and told each other enough news for a year ahead.
exact.Катушка шёлковых ниток, видишь, почти по: A spool of silk thread, see, nearly full. I'm saving it for something important, and in all these years nothing important has come along.
exact.У нас перемены шли с фабрик: сначала тка: For us change came from the factories: first the weaving mill, then the industrial zone, then the car factory. At home you knew how the street was doing by where people worked, and the mountain above the town stayed the same, only they ran a cable car up it.
exact.Как-то мы с сестрой поехали на гору смот: Once my sister and I went up the mountain to look at the snow and took nothing but bread and cheese. We got so cold we came down without a word, and at home we laughed till we cried remembering our noses.
exact.чайный стаканчик со щербинкой: a tea glass with a chip
exact.Чайный стаканчик, на краю щербинка. Из н: A tea glass, there's a chip on the rim. It's awkward to drink from, it scratches your lip, and I still pour mine into that one.
exact.Конья долго была наполовину городом, нап: For a long time Konya was half town, half village: lots of people had family in the villages round about and went visiting for flour. Then the town outgrew the villages, a university and new districts came, and the road to the family got longer, though not a single kilometre was added.
exact.Однажды я пекла лепёшки на всю родню и п: Once I baked flatbread for the whole family and put too much salt in the dough. Everyone ate it, nobody said a word, and a week later my aunt quietly brought me a new salt cellar.
exact.Мешочек из-под фисташек, холщовый. Фиста: A pistachio bag, a canvas one. The pistachios were eaten long ago, I keep buttons in it now, and they still smell a little of roasting.
exact.У нас перемены приходили фабриками на ок: For us change came as factories on the edge of town and the people who came to work in them. The town grew, the newcomers became neighbours and then relatives, and at the table people started arguing whose baklava was the proper one.
exact.Как-то я взялась сама жарить фисташки и: Once I took it into my head to roast pistachios myself and got so caught up talking to the neighbour that half of them burnt. She said they were even better that way, and we finished the lot, burnt ones too.
exact.кусочек угля в спичечном коробке: a piece of coal in a matchbox
exact.Вот спичечный коробок, а в нём кусочек у: Here's a matchbox, and there's a piece of coal in it. Funny, isn't it, keeping coal, but you couldn't explain this town without it.
exact.В Зонгулдаке всё зависело от шахт. Хозяе: In Zonguldak everything depended on the mines. The owners kept changing, a bank, then one administration, then another, and at home you found out by how and when the wages came and what the men said after their shift.
exact.Однажды я развесила бельё, и тут подул в: Once I'd just hung out the washing when the wind blew in from the mines. I had to wash the lot again, and I swore so much that the neighbour downstairs offered to let me hang it at hers, on the other side of the building.
exact.Тяжёлый болт, видишь, с заводской резьбо: A heavy bolt, see, with a factory thread. I use it to hold the papers down on the table so they don't blow away, I've never had a better paperweight.
exact.Карабюк вырос вокруг железной дороги и з: Karabük grew up around the railway and the works, before that there were just a few houses. At home we counted change by the shifts at the steelworks and by how many new shops had opened on our street.
exact.Как-то я решила испечь торт по рецепту и: Once I decided to bake a cake from a magazine recipe, and I didn't have the right tin. I baked it in a saucepan, it came out tall, lopsided and very tasty, and after that people ordered it from me for every birthday.
exact.Жестяная кружка, вся в царапинах. Из неё: A tin mug, all scratched. We drank water from it in the fields, by the canal, and I took it home once nobody minded if it wasn't returned.
exact.В Чумре всё решала вода: поля поливали и: In Çumra water decided everything: the fields were watered from canals, and the water came from Lake Beyşehir. At home we talked about water more than about the weather, and when the digs started nearby we joked that even the ancient people came here for the irrigation.
exact.Однажды мы с соседками пошли на базар в: Once the neighbours and I went to market in town and came back with a kid goat nobody had meant to buy. We argued all winter about how it happened, and the goat grew up and butted everyone without distinction.
exact.Шерстяной носок, недовязанный, спицы ещё: A woollen sock, unfinished, the needles are still in it. Our winters are long, and I always thought I'd finish it by the next one.
exact.У нас земля иногда напоминала о себе, зе: For us the earth sometimes reminded you it was there, everyone remembered the earthquakes. Otherwise change came quietly: villages went to new districts, the young left for the big cities, and the houses got roomier than you'd like.
exact.Как-то зимой замело так, что мы три дня: One winter we were snowed in so badly we didn't go out for three days, and the whole family played the same game till we'd all fallen out. On the fourth day we dug the door out, and to be honest I was a bit sorry.
exact.работница кондитерской фабрики Ülker: worker at the Ülker confectionery factory
exact.Меня взяли на кондитерскую фабрику Ülker: I got taken on at the Ülker confectionery factory, packing biscuits. The first week I brought broken bits home, and the little ones met me at the door like it was a holiday.
exact.Потом меня поставили старшей на линии. Я: Later they made me senior on the line. I could tell by the sound that the machine was about to start crushing packets, and I'd shout before it happened.
exact.На пенсию я ушла с фабрики. Печенье в ма: I retired from the factory. In the shop I still turn a packet of biscuits over and check whether it's sealed straight.
exact.ткачиха на текстильной фабрике в Бурсе: weaver at a textile mill in Bursa
exact.Я пошла на текстильную фабрику, в ткацки: I went to the textile mill, to the weaving shed. My first wage was small, but it was mine, and for a long time I didn't dare spend it.
exact.Со временем я вела несколько станков и п: In time I was running several looms and could tell by the clatter where a thread had snapped. The foreman grumbled that I noticed before he did, and I think it got to him.
exact.На пенсию я ушла с фабрики. Ткань я и те: I retired from the mill. I still rub fabric between my fingers first and only then look at the colour.
exact.служащая министерства в Анкаре: clerk at a ministry in Ankara
exact.После курсов делопроизводства меня взяли: After a records-keeping course I got a job at a ministry. Papers went from office to office for weeks, and at first I thought they had a life of their own.
exact.Скоро я знала, на каком столе какая папк: Soon I knew which desk a file would get stuck on and how to rescue it. The bosses changed, but that order stayed.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из министерства. Почерк: I retired from the ministry. My handwriting's been clerical ever since, even my holiday cards come out looking like certificates.
exact.лаборантка Эгейского университета в Изми: laboratory assistant at Ege University in İzmir
exact.После училища меня взяли лаборанткой в н: After college I was taken on as a lab assistant at the new university. Everything there was new, even the test tubes, and we handled them like crystal.
exact.Студенты менялись каждые несколько лет,: The students changed every few years, but I stayed and knew where everything was better than the professors. Sometimes they came to ask me and pretended they were checking.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из лаборатории. Банки н: I retired from the laboratory. The jars in my kitchen are still labelled, the neighbours laugh.
exact.Меня взяли в контору металлургического к: I got a job in the office of the steelworks, in the time office. I wrote down who'd come in for their shift, and the first month I mixed up the surnames: for a lot of people they were brand new then, and folk didn't always answer to them straight away.
exact.Со временем я знала рабочих по почерку н: In time I knew the workers by the handwriting on their forms and by the way they knocked on the hatch. The shops thundered behind the wall, and in our office the paper rustled.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из конторы комбината. Г: I retired from the steelworks office. I still hear the shift hooter in my sleep, though I've long lived where you can't hear it.
exact.счетоводка в конторе угольных шахт Зонгу: bookkeeper in the office of the Zonguldak coal mines
exact.После курсов счетоводства меня взяли в к: After a bookkeeping course I got a job in the office at the mines. I never once went underground, I counted tonnes and wages, but there was coal dust on my papers too.
exact.Хозяева у шахт за эти годы менялись, мен: Over the years the mines changed owners, the forms and stamps changed, but the figures were the same: how much was dug and how much was paid. I learnt to tell from a pay sheet which shift had been a hard one.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из конторы. Считаю я до: I retired from the office. I still do sums in a column on the edge of the newspaper, the neighbours' grandchildren watch it like a magic trick.
exact.работа на поливных полях в Чумре: work in the irrigated fields of Çumra
exact.Я работала на наших полях, как все в сем: I worked on our fields, like everyone in the family. The main thing was not to miss your turn for the water: oversleep, and your field stands dry while the neighbour's already watering.
exact.Со временем я сама знала, когда открыват: In time I knew myself when to open the channel and when to close it, and the men asked me, though they'd never admit it out loud.
exact.От полевой работы я отошла, когда стало: I gave up field work when it got too hard. But in the mornings I still look at the sky first thing and think about water.
exact.учительница сельской начальной школы: teacher at a village primary school
exact.После учительской школы меня послали в с: After teacher training I was sent to a village primary school. The letters were new, Latin ones, and sometimes my pupils' fathers came in the evening to learn from me too, more embarrassed than the children.
I ended up teaching the children of my first pupils. Parents didn't always let the girls come, and every autumn I went round the houses to talk them into it, with mixed success.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из школы. Бывшие ученик: I retired from the school. My former pupils still write to me, and to my shame I check their spelling.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, империя в: When I was very little, the empire went into the big war on Germany's side. I was told later that the men were taken into the army one after another.
exact.Началась большая война, империя воевала: The big war started, the empire was fighting on Germany's side. I remember the men leaving our street one after another, and suddenly there was a lot of women's work.
exact.Империя вступила в мировую войну на стор: The empire entered the world war on Germany's side, and a big mobilisation began. The men were taken one after another, and everything else was left to the women.
exact.Работу, которую раньше делали мужчины, т: Work the men used to do, we did now, and there was nobody to ask permission.
exact.Я не буду рассказывать того, чего не вид: I won't tell what I didn't see myself. What I remember most is the waiting: for letters, for news, for some kind of end.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, империя п: When I was very little, the empire signed an armistice and left the war. The grown-ups said later there was less relief than they'd expected.
exact.Осенью сказали, что война для нас кончил: In the autumn they said the war was over for us, an armistice had been signed. I expected everyone to cheer up at once, but for some reason the grown-ups got even quieter.
exact.В конце октября подписали перемирие, и и: At the end of October the armistice was signed and the empire left the war. A few days later the Young Turk leaders fled the country, and people didn't know whether to be glad or afraid.
exact.А потом в город вошли чужие войска, и к: And then foreign troops came into the town, and we had to get used to that somehow as well.
exact.Война кончилась, но никто не говорил, чт: The war was over, but nobody said everything would be fine now, they only said it would be different.
exact.Мир, который тогда наступил, был какой-т: The peace that came then felt somehow unfinished. Everyone was waiting for something, and the waiting went on for several more years.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, провозгла: When I was very little, the republic was proclaimed. I grew up in it, and for a long time it seemed to me it had never been any other way.
exact.Осенью объявили, что теперь у нас респуб: In the autumn they announced we were a republic now, and Mustafa Kemal had been elected president. I didn't really understand what it meant, but I remember how the grown-ups kept repeating that word.
exact.Двадцать девятого октября собрание прово: On the twenty-ninth of October the assembly proclaimed the republic, and Mustafa Kemal was elected its first president. Not long before, the capital had been moved inland, and people argued about that almost as hotly as about the republic.
exact.Слово «республика» стали говорить так ча: People said the word 'republic' so often that children put it into their games.
exact.Многие радовались, многие просто ждали,: Many were glad, many just waited to see what would come of it. Life doesn't change in a day, first the words change, and only then everything else.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, сменили б: When I was very little, they changed the letters, Latin ones instead of Arabic. I already learnt with the new ones, and only the older people at home could read the old letters.
exact.Нам сменили буквы, вместо арабских стали: They changed our letters, Latin instead of Arabic. It was funny that we children wrote the new ones faster than our parents.
exact.С первого ноября ввели новый алфавит, на: From the first of November a new alphabet came in, based on the Latin one. Newspapers, shop signs, school exercise books, everything went over to the new letters, and grown-ups were taught to read all over again.
exact.Старые книги в доме стали как будто на ч: The old books at home seemed to be in a foreign language, though the language was the same.
exact.Мама сидела вечерами над букварём вместе: Mum sat over the primer with me in the evenings and got cross when I corrected her. Some never quite relearnt it, and the neighbours read their letters out to them.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, женщинам: When I was very little, women were allowed to vote in parliamentary elections and to stand for parliament themselves. I grew up knowing that, and for a long time I didn't understand why the grown-ups were so pleased about it.
exact.Взрослые говорили, что теперь женщины то: The grown-ups said that now women chose the parliament too and could even get into it. My friends and I straight away decided which of us would be a deputy.
exact.В декабре женщинам дали право голосовать: In December women got the right to vote in parliamentary elections and to be elected, and in local elections women had been voting for several years already. In February eighteen women entered the assembly.
exact.Мама стала читать газету до конца, а не: Mum started reading the newspaper to the end, not just the notices.
exact.Одни радовались, другие ворчали, что это: Some were glad, others grumbled that it wasn't women's business, and then nearly everyone who was allowed went to vote. I didn't think for a long time about how recently that had become normal for us.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, всем веле: When I was very little, everyone was told to take a surname. I was told later how ours was chosen and how they nearly fell out over it.
exact.Вышел закон, и всем велели взять фамилии: A law came out, and everyone was told to take a surname. I remember the grown-ups going through words at supper, and it felt to me like they were choosing a new name for the whole family.
exact.Летом вышел закон, что у всех должны быт: In the summer a law came out that everyone must have a surname, and titles like 'bey' and 'pasha' were abolished. You had to choose a surname and register it, and every family argued about it.
exact.В школе и в бумагах всех стали звать по-: At school and on paper everyone was called something new, and at first people didn't always answer to their own surname.
exact.В одних семьях выбирали долго и всерьёз,: Some families chose for a long time and very seriously, others took the first thing that came into their heads. The neighbours laughed at some surnames for years, and then they got used to them, and so did the people who carried them.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, шла больш: When I was very little, there was a big war on, but our country stayed out of it almost the whole time. The grown-ups said later they lived waiting all the same.
exact.Шла большая война, а наша страна держала: There was a big war on and our country was keeping out of it, and the grown-ups were afraid it wouldn't manage to. Near the end war on Germany was declared after all, when it was already finishing.
exact.Почти всю большую войну страна держалась: For almost the whole big war the country kept out of it. In February forty-five it did declare war on Germany and Japan, and in the autumn Turkey became one of the countries that founded the UN.
exact.Радио стали слушать по-другому, уже не с: People started listening to the radio differently, not in fear any more, but to find out what the world would be like next.
exact.Мы жили рядом с войной, но не в ней, и э: We lived next to the war but not in it, and it's a strange feeling: you're listening out all the time. I don't want to tell what I don't know, but everyone was anxious in those years.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, на выбора: When I was very little, the opposition won an election for the first time, and power changed hands peacefully. I know that from what people told me.
exact.Весной были выборы, и победила Демократи: In the spring there was an election, and the Democrat Party won. The grown-ups argued so much that I realised for the first time elections aren't just for choosing a class monitor.
exact.В мае пятидесятого на выборах победила Д: In May fifty the Democrat Party won the election, and for the first time power passed peacefully to the opposition. Many didn't believe that could happen till they saw it for themselves.
exact.О политике стали спорить вслух, на базар: People started arguing about politics out loud, at the market and when visiting, and didn't always stop in time.
exact.Кто-то радовался, кто-то тревожился, а у: Some were glad, some were worried, and at home we were split almost down the middle. That was the first time I felt something could depend on one slip of paper.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, армия взя: When I was very little, the army took power. I only know that from what people told me.
exact.В мае армия взяла власть, и взрослые дол: In May the army took power, and the grown-ups listened to the radio in silence for a long time.
exact.В конце мая шестидесятого армия взяла вл: At the end of May sixty the army took power, and the president and the prime minister were removed. A year and a half later power went back to civilians, but everyone remembered that time differently.
exact.Новости по радио с тех пор слушали внима: After that people listened to the news on the radio more closely than before and asked each other what they'd heard.
exact.Об этом у нас говорили осторожно и по-ра: At home people talked about it carefully and in different ways, and I won't pass judgement. I just remember how many rumours there were and how few people knew anything for sure.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, подписали: When I was very little, an agreement was signed and people started going to work in West Germany. All my life after that I knew someone who lived there.
exact.Подписали договор с Западной Германией,: An agreement was signed with West Germany, and people started going there to work. I remember the neighbours seeing their people off with suitcases and promising it wouldn't be for long.
exact.В конце октября шестьдесят первого подпи: At the end of October sixty-one an agreement was signed with West Germany to recruit workers. People went off to earn money, they thought for a year or two, and many stayed for good.
exact.В разговорах появилось слово «Алманья»,: The word 'Almanya' came into every conversation, and letters from there were read out to everyone nearby.
exact.Уезжали и мужчины, и женщины, а приезжал: Both men and women went, and when they came back on holiday they were already a bit different, with suitcases of presents and new habits. Some meant to come back all their lives, and their children already thought in two languages.
exact.В конце семидесятых всего не хватало, лю: At the end of the seventies there wasn't enough of anything, people queued. I know that from what people told me.
exact.В конце семидесятых за маслом и газом ст: At the end of the seventies people queued for cooking oil and gas. They'd send me to keep our place, and I heard all the news there before the grown-ups did.
exact.В конце семидесятых всё вдруг стало в де: At the end of the seventies everything was suddenly in short supply: people queued for cooking oil, cigarettes, bottled gas, petrol. Prices went up so fast there was no point remembering them.
exact.Я привыкла держать дома запас масла и вс: I got used to keeping a stock of oil at home and always knew who round about had a spare gas bottle.
exact.Очередь была и наказанием, и клубом, там: The queue was a punishment and a club at once, that's where you heard all the news. People were angry with everyone at once, and brought home both oil and gossip.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, армия сно: When I was very little, the army took power again. I know that from what people told me.
exact.В сентябре армия взяла власть, и по всей: In September the army took power, and martial law was declared all over the country. The grown-ups started talking more quietly, even at home.
exact.Двенадцатого сентября восьмидесятого арм: On the twelfth of September eighty the army took power again, and martial law was declared in every province. Elections only came back three years later, under a new constitution.
exact.Разговоры о политике дома стали короче,: Talk about politics at home got shorter, and the streets were quieter in the evenings.
exact.Оценивать я не возьмусь, у каждого своя: I won't take it on myself to judge, everyone has their own memory of those years. Some remembered later that things got calmer, others remembered what they'd had to stop talking about.
exact.В девяносто четвёртом был тяжёлый кризис: In ninety-four there was a bad crisis, prices doubled. I know that from what people told me.
exact.В девяносто четвёртом цены росли так быс: In ninety-four prices went up so fast that the grown-ups stopped talking about them and just sighed at the counter.
exact.В девяносто четвёртом экономика сжалась,: In ninety-four the economy shrank, and prices more than doubled in a year. Wages and pensions melted away before they reached your purse.
exact.Я стала покупать всё сразу в день пенсии: I started buying everything at once on pension day, while the money was still worth something.
exact.Мы считали в миллионах и всё равно ничег: We counted in millions and still couldn't afford anything, it was almost funny. We laughed, but we still remembered the prices, so we'd have something to complain about.
exact.В девяносто девятом под Измитом было стр: In ninety-nine there was a terrible earthquake near İzmit. I know that from what people told me.
exact.Летом ночью случилось большое землетрясе: One summer night there was a big earthquake by the Sea of Marmara. For weeks afterwards the grown-ups didn't turn the television off.
exact.Семнадцатого августа, в три часа ночи, з: On the seventeenth of August, at three in the morning, an earthquake near İzmit destroyed towns all round the Sea of Marmara. More than eighteen thousand people died, hundreds of thousands were left homeless, and for weeks the whole country lived with nothing else.
exact.Я после этого долго спала, поставив у кр: For a long time after that I slept with my shoes by the bed and a torch beside them.
exact.Мы смотрели новости и не могли оторватьс: We watched the news and couldn't tear ourselves away, we rang everyone we could get through to. I won't go into details, I'll only say that people helped each other however they could, and I remember that too.
